title: Near ground in the game vs the editor: DXT colour-map rounding and resized water drawn as a 1000 m sheet (2026-11-16)

facts.title: The PC game draws a scenario colour map saved as swizzled A8R8G8B8 (fmt 06) exactly; DXT colour maps shift dark ground colours by up to 8 levels per channel
facts.fact: Retail and older editor saves write the colour map as DXT5. Its 5:6:5 endpoints round a dark ground colour (Under Cover greens about 24-48) by up to 8 levels per channel: a faint tint gradient (R 28-31 against G 29) came back as bands of (24,28,16) olive and (33,28,16) brown, 202 of 32,768 texels off, up to 14 levels, 19 with red / green order flipped. A colour map saved as swizzled A8R8G8B8 with the level's size and mips (128 x 256, Under Cover base) loads in PC Release 1.0.9: the lit terrain draw binds it as t0 fmt 06 and RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE_TEXDUMP of t0 equals the editor's colour map byte for byte (131,072 bytes, 0 different).
facts.how_to_use: Editor saves the colour map as A8R8G8B8 (core/scenario.cpp colormap_game_layout). A few hundred KB of graphics memory more per map.

facts.title: A resized Env_Water1000x1000 water (MA2SE_._WxL model) is drawn by the PC game with vertices hundreds of metres away: a sheet at the water height over flat banks, darkening the near ground about 2x
facts.fact: P8 copy (Under Cover base, flat ground 10.12, three resized waters of Env_Water1000x1000 at height 10.12 / 6: 176 x 24 at (432, 300), 80 x 60 at (620, 300), 176 x 32 at (610, 420)). Player at (380, 262), 26 m from the nearest water edge. Frame trace (PC Release, pixel 486,384 of 640x480, flat ground about 11 m ahead): terrain base (72,70,30), micro pass (98,90,34), then the water passes (prog 01022 normal write, prog 64621, prog 00421 with t0 = frame copy, t2 = ground light map) cover the pixel and leave (49,45,15); the water draw's vertex 0 is 541-544 m from the eye (w). With the three waters deleted the same spot shows the ground as the editor does (no water draws on the pixel; region luma ratio editor / game 0.87 vs 1.8 with water). Renaming the generated mesh / vertex / index entries (so they cannot collide with the shipped template model's 'water_1000x1000' names) did NOT change it (vertex 0 still 541 m). Cause open: the game seems to draw the template's 1000 x 1000 grid (or a plane from another source) at the instance's height.
facts.how_to_use: Open for the game tree: dump the water draw's vertices (RECOMP_FRAME_TRACE_VERTICES) and check which model the MAWater instance draws. Until then a resized water on ground at its own height darkens the banks in the game only.
